subject: How to consider plots and areas???

messages.author: 027ebd52b68c9065
messages.subject: How to consider plots and areas???
parts:
Hello,

I'm new to SEM language and I'm still learning about ...

I'm working with the growth of plants, planted in different areas. To collect data, we have established some plots in each area.

I have a question about how to consider plant growth within the same plots and within the same areas (as they are more related than plants of other plots and areas), on SEM?

Should it be a case of nested models? Or multiple groups models?
Considering the plots and the areas as blocks (treatments)?

Any help will be greatly appreciated !!!

Very Grateful
Kind Regards
Gabriel

messages.author: 253141a6efac547e
messages.subject: Re: How to consider plots and areas???
parts: There are two good options. First, check out the lavaan.survey package for this type of data using the covariance based approach. If you are more comfortable with mixed models, check out the piecewiseSEM package and accompanying papers.

Just another question, as I have seen shortly, the piecewiseSEM package seems not being flexible with composite and latente variables. Is that true?

Grateful
Regards,
Gabriel
2017-06-09 18:30 GMT-07:00 Jarrett Byrnes <jarrett...@gmail.com>:

There are two good options. First, check out the lavaan.survey package for this type of data using the covariance based approach. If you are more comfortable with mixed models, check out the piecewiseSEM package and accompanying papers.
